Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajesh Shankar For
the Petitioner : Mr. Nilesh Kumar, Advocate For the State : Ms. Nehala Sharmin, A.P.P. For the O.P.
No. 2 : Mr. Rahul Kumar (in person) Order No. 08 Dated: 14.08.2024
The petitioner apprehending his arrest for the offences punishable under Sections 420/406/467/468/471 of the Indian Penal Code, has prayed for grant of anticipatory bail.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case and has not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.

As per the allegation, a person namely Ajay Kumar by showing himself to be the son of Harlal Prasad (who is in fact the father of the informant/opposite party no. 2) and showing Lila Prasad (mother of the opposite party no. 2) as dead, executed general power of attorney in favour of the petitioner with respect to 13.50 acres of land appertaining to Plot Nos. 2414, 2411, 2409, 2412, 2413, 2410 and 2406 all belonging to Khata No. 395 situated at village Hutap, P.S - Chandwa, District - Latehar.
The said lands thereafter were sold by the petitioner in favour of his family members and relatives by three different sale deeds and at present, their names are being shown in Register-II.
3. It is further submitted that there is no forgery on the part of the petitioner in execution of the said general power of attorney.

If at all, co-accused Ajay Kumar had executed the general power of attorney with respect to the lands in question in favour of the petitioner impersonating himself to be the son of the actual recorded tenant of the said lands i.e., Harlal Prasad, the petitioner himself is a victim of said mischievous act.
Moreover, if the petitioner had any fraudulent intention to grab the lands of the father of the opposite party no. 2, he would not have sold the same in favour of his family members and relatives.
Even on perusal of the written report, it would be evident that the main allegation is against co-accused Ajay Kumar.
Though the present F.I.R. was lodged on 05.07.2023, however no cogent evidence has been collected by the police to connect the petitioner with the alleged offence.
The petitioner has been implicated in the present case merely on suspicion.

sentences.text: 1 Moreover, the dispute raised by the opposite party no. 2 in the F.I.R is civil in nature and he could have moved before the Civil Court seeking cancellation of the sale deeds, if the same were fraudulently executed.
As per the well settled principle of law, there is a presumption that a registered document is validly executed and the onus of proof is on the person who claims to rebut the said presumption.
Nonetheless, in the case in hand, the informant/opposite party no. 2 has not been able to present any cogent evidence so as to connect the petitioner with the alleged offence.
The petitioner is a businessman and is ready to cooperate in the ongoing investigation.
The petitioner has no criminal antecedent as has been stated in paragraph-11 of the present anticipatory bail application.
Hence, he may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

4. The opposite party no.2, who appears in person, while opposing the petitioner's prayer for anticipatory bail, submits that the petitioner in connivance with co-accused Ajay Kumar (who may not be actual person in existence) has grabbed 13.50 acres of valuable land of his father.

However,
the counter affidavit filed by the opposite party no. 2 does not disclose as to in what manner, the petitioner conspired with co-accused Ajay Kumar in getting the general power of attorney executed in his favour.

5. Learned A.P.P. also opposes the petitioner's prayer for anticipatory bail and submits that despite several notices issued to the petitioner under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C., he is neither responding the same nor appearing before the concerned I.O.
6.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the materials available on record, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on anticipatory bail.

7. Accordingly, the petitioner, above named, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the court below within three weeks from today, shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Latehar in connection with Chandwa P.S. Case No. 141 of 2023 with the conditions that the petitioner will co-operate in the investigation of the case and will appear before the concerned Investigating Officer as and when noticed by him.

The petitioner will also furnish his mobile number and photocopy of 'Aadhar Card' at the time of surrender in the court below with an undertaking that he will not change his mobile number during the pendency of the case and subject to further conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Ritesh/
